summary: Addendum covering August versions of GPT-5.6 Sol and Luna deployed in ChatGPT, replacing GPT-5.5 Instant (including a new Free/Go default). Reports disallowed content (first dedicated under-18 evaluations), vision, dynamic mental health, jailbreaks, prompt injection, HealthBench, hallucination, and Preparedness bio/cyber evals and model-refusal safeguard evals; safety evals measured at lowest deployed reasoning setting.

framework.name: Preparedness Framework
framework.level_or_determination: High in Biological and Chemical and High in Cybersecurity (below Critical); below High in AI Self-Improvement
framework.quote: we have determined that the updated GPT-5.6 Sol and GPT-5.6 Luna models for ChatGPT warrant the same Preparedness Framework designations as the previously released GPT-5.6 models: High in Biological and Chemical, High in Cybersecurity, and below High in AI Self-Improvement.

evals: DNA sequence design for TF binding
cbrn_bio_chem.finding: Both models treated High; AAV capsid eval skipped because majority rule already settled Critical determination.
cbrn_bio_chem.quote: Under the currently applicable majority rule, the remaining AAV result could not change the overall determination, so the evaluation team concluded that an additional AAV assessment was not necessary.

cyber.finding: Evaluated on near-final representative checkpoints; both High, below Critical by similarity to July versions. Luna below High threshold on CVE-Bench. Two saturated range scenarios deprecated.
cyber.quote: The updated GPT-5.6 Sol and GPT-5.6 Luna models were determined to be below Critical, as the measured capabilities are similar to their previously released counterparts, which are also below Critical.

autonomy_ai_rnd.finding: Not run; capabilities similar to July release.
autonomy_ai_rnd.quote: AI Self-Improvement capability evals were not run, as GPT-5.6 Sol has similar capabilities to July release across several intelligence evaluations and was considered below High Capability.

harmful_content_refusal.finding: Sol comparable to GPT-5.5 Instant June Update except gore and sexual content; Luna except gore.
harmful_content_refusal.quote: We find that GPT-5.6 Sol performs comparably (i.e., no statistically significant difference) to the previous production ChatGPT (GPT-5.5 Instant June Update) model on all disallowed categories with the exception of gore and disallowed sexual content.

over_refusal.finding: Benign over-refusal row not reported in this addendum.

evals: multiturn jailbreak eval (worst-case defender success rate)
jailbreak_robustness.quote: GPT-5.6 Sol and GPT-5.6 Luna perform comparably to recent predecessors.

prompt_injection.finding: On par with previous Instant models.
prompt_injection.quote: GPT-5.6 Sol and GPT-5.6 Luna both perform on-par with previous Instant models.

metrics.name: Factual error reduction vs GPT-5.5 Instant (Sol)

honesty_hallucination.finding: Substantial factuality improvements for both models.
honesty_hallucination.quote: GPT-5.6 Sol delivers statistically significant and more consistent improvements overall, reducing factual error rates by roughly 60% across all three prompt sets.

evals: U18 disallowed-content evaluations (age-restricted goods/dangerous challenges, sexual content, eating disorders, emotional reliance, self-harm, gore)
child_safety.finding: First dedicated U18 evals; strong performance with gains on age-restricted goods and sexual content, no statistically significant differences vs GPT-5.5 variants.
child_safety.quote: For the first time, we are including dedicated U18 evaluations designed to measure model behavior against teen-specific safety standards.

evals: Dynamic Mental Health Benchmarks with Adversarial User Simulations
U18 emotional reliance / self harm / eating disorders
self_harm_wellbeing.finding: Largely comparable except statistically significant self-harm regression; no increase seen in online experimentation.
self_harm_wellbeing.quote: We find that GPT-5.6 Sol is largely comparable on these evaluations to GPT-5.5 Instant June Update, with the exception of statistically significant regression on the self-harm evaluation.

system_safeguards.finding: Same safeguards as GPT-5.6 system card; model-level refusal on par with July release.
system_safeguards.quote: The updated GPT-5.6 Sol and GPT-5.6 Luna models for ChatGPT are deployed with the respective safeguards developed for the previous models.

notable_new_eval_methods: Safety evals measured at lowest deployed reasoning setting; capabilities at max effort (p.2)
Majority-rule skipping of AAV Critical eval (p.21)

self_reported_limitations.text: Earlier Standard disallowed-content evals had become relatively saturated.
Jailbreak results directional rather than definitive.
Disparities between offline mental-health evals and online testing under investigation.
Cyber evals run on near-final representative checkpoints rather than launch models.
Printer Queue and Simple Privilege Escalation range scenarios deprecated due to heavy saturation.
U18 evals focus on difficult cases and should not be read as production frequency estimates.

notes: No alignment, CoT, metagaming or third-party evaluation sections in this addendum (relies on GPT-5.6 system card).
